hook.pre: Recognised as a sport in Brazil
hook.line: Football played by flicking buttons — in Brazil an officially recognised sport.
hook.say: Football with buttons! Let me show you Brazil’s game!

ch.say: It all started in children’s pockets.
p: Button football is said to have begun in the early 1900s, with children in Brazil, Hungary and elsewhere flicking coat buttons and bottle caps. In Brazil the painter and actor Geraldo Décourt turned it into a sport: in 1930 he published the first rule book, the official rules of “Foot-Ball Celotex”.

Celotex was the fibreboard that covered the tables. The São Paulo state federation was founded in 1962, and in 1988 Brazil’s National Sports Council recognised “futebol de mesa” (table football) as an official sport. Décourt’s birthday, 14 February, is Button Player’s Day in São Paulo state.

ch.cap: The field: 167 cm long, 104 cm wide, a goal at each end
p: An official table is about 183 × 120 cm, with a field 167 cm long and 104 cm wide painted on it. Each side has ten discs 3.5–6 cm across and a goalkeeper, a block 8 × 3.5 cm. The ball is a felt ball 1 cm across (a little bigger here, so you can see it).

Brazil has several rule sets; this game follows the 12-touch rule: up to 12 touches each time you have the ball, no more than 3 in a row with one button. A shot is called before it is taken, and the defender sets the goalkeeper.

ch.say: The number of touches changes everything!
